kernel: the row-exact 4/6/8-bit affine quantized matmul pair, TensorFold ports: simd_qmm (one fixed FMA chain per 64-input group, groups split over S chunks combined by a fixed tree, 8x8 fp32 simdgroup_matrix mma for 2 or more rows with a per-pass pre-scaled activation fragment, a scalar one-row form, a row-staged scalar variant, and a per-shape prepare probe) and rowqmv (MLX's qmv_fast loop, one input row per simdgroup, 4 output rows per simdgroup)
summary: Serves every decode-width affine projection of 1 to 16 rows on a trunk with ModelConfig.rowExactDecode set (dense qwen3_5 or nemotron_h, no Hadamard pack, a DFlash drafter bound), so serial-decode rows, MTP rows and DFlash verify/tree rows all get the one-row step's bits. simd_qmm splits a row's K/64 groups over S shape-only chunks (16 for N <= 2048, else 8) combined in a fixed order: mma for 2 or more rows (frag over prep-staged fragments at 2 to 8), a scalar form for one row, a row-staged scalar variant at 2 to 3 rows at 4 bits; a per-shape probe routes one-row calls through mma where the chip's mma differs from the scalar chain. rowqmv is the fallback: MLX's qmv_fast loop with each input row on its own simdgroup. Under rowExactDecode it serves both decode and verify rows; without a drafter, batched decode takes it only from 8 rows where no matmul2d tile exists.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.quant: MLX affine 4-bit, group 64, bf16 scales and biases (the kernels also take 6 and 8 bits)

models.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B
models.quant: 2-bit ternary affine pack; its DFlash2 drafter linears are load-time quantized to bf16 affine so the bf16-only row kernels accept them
models.role: secondary (drafter path behind the measured 22.5 tok/s result)

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 (nemotron_h)
models.quant: affine 4/6/8-bit, group 32/64/128 through the rowqmv path
models.role: gate-covered family; its projection shapes are the rowqmv test shapes (src/rowqmv.zig:469)

settings.name: row_exact_max_rows
settings.condition: simd_qmm.qmm and rowqmv.qmv, experts and router row count
settings.note: same bound in src/rowqmv.zig:7; x is reshaped to [rows, K] at src/simd_qmm.zig:622 and back after

settings.name: quant_bits_supported
settings.note: rowqmv's check at src/rowqmv.zig:142

settings.name: group_size_simd_qmm
settings.condition: simd_qmm only; other group sizes decline

settings.name: group_sizes_rowqmv
settings.note: a pack at group 32 or 128 routes to rowqmv under the gate, not simd_qmm

settings.name: k_multiple
settings.note: simd_qmm: ws[1] * 32 % (64 * bits) == 0; rowqmv: (last-dim * 32 / bits) % 64 == 0 at src/rowqmv.zig:149

settings.name: n_multiple
settings.note: rowqmv at src/rowqmv.zig:149

settings.name: operand_dtypes
settings.value: w uint32, scales and biases bfloat16, x bfloat16
settings.note: rowqmv at src/rowqmv.zig:144; x dtype at src/simd_qmm.zig:594 and src/rowqmv.zig:165; the Bonsai f16-scale incident was exactly a bf16-only decline

settings.name: split_chunks_n_le_2048
settings.note: capped at 16 because mma runs S simdgroups per threadgroup and a 1024-thread group exceeds what older GPUs grant this kernel (comment at src/simd_qmm.zig:400-401)

settings.name: split_chunks_n_gt_2048
settings.note: splits(n) is a function of the shape only, which is what pins a row's bits

settings.name: fma_chain_per_group
settings.value: 64 fmas per 64-input group: 8 passes s of 8 inputs i, one fixed (s, i) order shared by scalar, rows, mma and frag
settings.note: the row-staged variant keeps the one-row chain per row and builds the masked weight fields once per pass across rows (comment and loop at src/simd_qmm.zig:182-194)

settings.name: activation_pre_scale
settings.value: wpre = 2^-(4*p) per pass p at 4 bits, 2^-(8*(p mod 4)) at 8 bits, written as exponent-bias 127-e << 23; 1.0 at 6 bits
settings.condition: activation fragment of pass s, all kinds
settings.note: pre-scaling the input cancels the in-place mask shift so no shift rides the dot; applied at src/simd_qmm.zig:80 (scalar staging) and 341-342 (mma fragment)

settings.name: six_bit_field_decode
settings.value: 6-bit codes straddle 32-bit words: field shifted down to 0..63 with a carry from the next word, so wpre stays 1

settings.name: mma_fragment_form
settings.value: 8x8 fp32 simdgroup_matrix accumulators, one per (row tile, output tile); the weight fragment am is built per (pass, output tile) and reused across the row tiles via simdgroup_multiply_accumulate
settings.note: accumulate at src/simd_qmm.zig:285; per-group scale/bias at 294-295; the frag variant reads prep-staged pre-scaled fragments instead of re-reading x per threadgroup (src/simd_qmm.zig:345-359)

settings.name: mma_row_tiles_max
settings.condition: mma and frag; rowTiles = min(RT_MAX, ceil(rows / 8))
settings.note: rowTiles formula at src/simd_qmm.zig:407

settings.name: mma_output_tiles
settings.value: 4 when N % 32 == 0, 2 when N % 16 == 0, else 1; halved while S * row_tiles * nt * 64 floats would exceed 16384 bytes of threadgroup reduction
settings.note: 16 KB cap at src/simd_qmm.zig:414

settings.name: staging_block_groups
settings.condition: scalar, rows and mma input staging blocks
settings.note: the rows variant shrinks the block to the largest multiple of S fitting 32 KB so each chunk still visits its groups in order (src/simd_qmm.zig:503-506)

settings.name: rows_staging_bytes
settings.condition: row-staged scalar variant: rows * splits(n) * 76 floats must fit
settings.note: past it the kind pick falls to mma/frag even below the row cap (src/simd_qmm.zig:617)

settings.name: scalar_rows_max_4bit
settings.condition: 4-bit; at 6 and 8 bits only one row takes scalar
settings.note: selection rows_max = (bits == 4) ? SCALAR_ROWS_MAX : 1 at src/simd_qmm.zig:616; their comment: past it mma is cheaper, and at 6 and 8 bits from two rows (src/simd_qmm.zig:395-396)

settings.name: fragment_rows_max
settings.condition: rows 2..8 read prep-staged fragments; past that plain mma
settings.note: kind pick at src/simd_qmm.zig:617-618; prep writes pre-scaled fragments once per (row tile, group), one simdgroup each (src/simd_qmm.zig:364-390)

settings.name: scalar_simdgroups
settings.value: 8 simdgroups per threadgroup at N <= 2048, 2 at N > 2048; 1 output row per lane at N <= 2048, 2 above
settings.note: constants SGS 2 and NR 2 at src/simd_qmm.zig:13-14

settings.name: combine_tree
settings.value: cross-lane sum by simd_shuffle_xor fma pairs at offsets 1, 2, 4, ... ascending (scalar); mma folds its S partials pairwise v[k] = fma(v[k+w], one, v[k]) with w doubling 1, 2, 4, 8
settings.condition: after the per-chunk group walk, every kind
settings.note: mma form at src/simd_qmm.zig:316-317; halving the simdgroups per threadgroup keeps this order, so the bits do not change (test at src/simd_qmm.zig:705-734)

settings.name: per_group_scale_bias
settings.value: acc = fma(fp32(scale_g), P_g, acc) then acc = fma(fp32(bias_g), xsum_g, acc), groups ascending within a chunk, one fp32 accumulator per row
settings.condition: every kind; the row's group sum rides the bias term
settings.note: mma form at src/simd_qmm.zig:294-295; bf16 store of the fp32 accumulator at src/simd_qmm.zig:125

settings.name: probe_rows
settings.condition: prepare, once per (N, K, bits) shape on the first simd_qmm call of any kind
settings.note: 8 random normal f32 rows (sd 0.5, mlx_random_key seed 0x5eed at src/simd_qmm.zig:643) cast to bf16; all 8 run through mma, each row also through a one-row scalar call, compared with mlx_array_equal (src/simd_qmm.zig:654-668); any mismatch marks the shape mma_one_row (src/simd_qmm.zig:670), which routes that shape's one-row calls through mma from then on; a shape whose kernel fails is recorded in declined and never re-probed (src/simd_qmm.zig:606-615)

settings.name: rowqmv_rows_per_simdgroup
settings.condition: every rowqmv launch; one input row per simdgroup, the row count a launch dimension only
settings.note: structure comment at src/rowqmv.zig:87-88; grid (32 * rows, N / 4) at src/rowqmv.zig:127

settings.name: rowqmv_lane_load
settings.value: 16 inputs per lane per block at 4 bits, 8 at 6 and 8 bits (VPL)

settings.name: rowqmv_block_inputs
settings.value: 32 lanes * VPL: 512 inputs per block at 4 bits, 256 at 6 and 8 bits; a K tail below one block runs one more chunk on the first (K % block) / VPL lanes
settings.note: tail at src/rowqmv.zig:77-81

settings.name: rowqmv_predivide
settings.value: inputs pre-divided per nibble lane (4-bit: 16, 256, 4096; 6-bit: 64, 16, 4) so masked weight fields need no shift; the 4/6-bit dot adds each run of 4 in bf16 first as MLX does on bfloat16_t, the 8-bit one adds each input in fp32
settings.note: 6-bit per-byte masks at src/rowqmv.zig:41-51

settings.name: output_dtype
settings.condition: both kernels store the fp32 accumulator rounded once to bf16
settings.note: rowqmv output arg at src/rowqmv.zig:125; stores at src/simd_qmm.zig:125 and src/rowqmv.zig:101

gates.condition: rowExactDecode: row_exact_covered and dflash_bound and rowExactArch; while it holds every decode-width affine projection takes the row-exact kernels, otherwise stock paths
rowExactArch: model_type nemotron_h, or a qwen3_5 prefix that is not MoE and has hadamard_block == 0 (no Hadamard rotation pack)

row_exact_covered is set at load only when rowExactArch holds and firstRowExactMiss finds no weight outside the kernels; a miss logs '[row-exact] ... outside the row kernels' and verify rows stay non-byte-exact
in Transformer.qmatmul: format engines (GGUF, sushi fp8, int8/Hadamard, ternary) run first; rowExactQmm only when rowExactDecode and mode == affine; stock qmatmulBits after

rowExactQmm pick: dense qwen3_5 tries lane_qmm on NAX hosts, then simd_qmm; rowqmv.qmv is the fallback and serves nemotron_h directly (its thin MoE trunk streams faster through per-row matvecs); the pick follows the weight and the GPU, never the row count
gates.note: fallback at src/transformer.zig:36697; nemotron_h branch at 36692

gates.condition: simd_qmm declines (returns null): non-GPU stream, fits false, non-bf16 x, K * bits mismatch, rows outside 1..16, or a shape in the declined map
gates.note: rows check at 603, declined check at 606, probe-failure recording at 607-615

gates.condition: kind pick inside simd_qmm: probe-flagged shapes, rows past rows_max, or staging overflow take mma (frag at 2..8 rows); otherwise scalar at 1 row and the row-staged variant at 2..3 rows (4-bit)
the probe switches one-row calls of a shape to mma where this GPU's mma bits differ from scalar's; it runs once per (N, K, bits) on the first call of any kind
gates.note: probe body at src/simd_qmm.zig:635-671, first-call hook at 607

gates.condition: batched decode without a drafter: simd_qmm from 8 rows where no matmul2d verify tile exists, off where one does; MLX_SERVE_SIMD_QMM_DECODE=N overrides (0 = off)
the drafter-side projection path (projectWithConfig) applies the same rowExactDecode gate

measured.conditions: their reference: 'exact mode costs MTP ~30%, so MTP/serial stay stock', the reason serial decode and MTP rounds keep stock paths unless a DFlash drafter is bound

measured.model: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B 2-bit with z-lab's bf16 DFlash2 drafter
measured.conditions: code 24.6, math 29.7, prose 13.3; the M4 MMA lane with block 8 as the default, after the f16/bf16 drafter dtype fix that had made simd_qmm decline (14.6 before); assist 13.5 ms, head 7.4 ms, peak 9.4 GB

measured.model: Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit (the lane_qmm NAX arm of the same row-exact contract, not simd_qmm)
measured.conditions: vs TensorFold 0.5.0's 241 in the same session, llmprobe --runs 2; prefill 1936 vs 1691, 8k/16k rungs 179-196 / 177-181 vs 166 / 163, 6-bit decode 190 vs 166, 8-bit 168 vs 159

notes: Doc-vs-source: our section says the mma 'weight fragment built once per group and reused across row tiles'; the source builds the weight fragment per (pass, output tile) and reuses it across the two row tiles (src/simd_qmm.zig:280-285), and the row-staged scalar variant builds masked weight fields once per pass across staged rows (src/simd_qmm.zig:189-194) - sided with the source. Our section calls rowqmv 'the fallback when simd_qmm declines a shape or its probe fails'; the source also tries lane_qmm before simd_qmm on NAX hosts and serves nemotron_h through rowqmv directly rather than as a fallback (src/transformer.zig:36692-36697). The 448-thread M1/M2 threadgroup cap for this kernel family is a source comment (src/simd_qmm.zig:430-431); the source shows only the halving fallback on a 'Thread group size' eval error (src/simd_qmm.zig:567-578), not our doc's 448-or-704 range, and the halving keeps the chunk walk order so the bits do not change. Our line 'This is simdgroup_matrix, so it runs on the M4 Max' is not shown by this file: simd_qmm names no chip; the mma_sg map exists because some GPUs cap the threadgroup and the probe exists because some chips' mma does not reproduce the scalar chain, so the M4 Max claim rests on their release notes, not the kernel source. The probe runs on the first call of any kind for a shape (src/simd_qmm.zig:607), not only before the first one-row call. simd_qmm requires group size 64 while rowqmv admits 32, 64 and 128, so a 32- or 128-group pack under the gate routes to rowqmv. rowqmv also carries routed-expert up/down kernels with fused relu2 and a dense bf16 router on the same one-simdgroup-per-row contract (src/rowqmv.zig:274, 334); they are outside this matmul entry's scope but share the contract and the gate. All three measured figures were found only in the repo's docs (docs/reference.md:814, docs/reference.md:558, docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:5595), not in the kernel files, and none carries a protocol or seed detail beyond the conditions listed.
